articles.title: I built a generic multi-step flow engine on top of Laravel controllers
articles.summary: At Zeney Pay we build a mobile app for cross-border money transfers and real-time currency conversion. A fintech backend is mostly flows: sign-in with 2FA, registration, KYC, "forgot my PIN", setting up a transaction PIN, sending money. None of them fit in a single HTTP request. For a while we handled them the way most teams do, and it went badly. This post covers what went wrong, how we changed our thinking, the design decisions behind the result, and the package that came out of it: na2axl/laravel-api-flow. How it went wrong Our flows were spread out in two ways: On the backend, one flow was split across several controllers. AuthController@login, OtpController@verify, PinController@check... Each endpoint had to work out for itself whether the caller had actually gone through the earlier steps. On the frontend, the mobile app held the rest. It decided which screen came next, when to skip the OTP screen, and what "back" meant. This gave us several sources of truth for the same business

articles.title: I Built a Stock Price Prediction App While Learning ML — Here's What I Learned
articles.summary: TL;DR: I built a full-stack stock prediction app with 7 ML algorithms, 1,001 stocks, and offline-first support. It's open source, and I'd love your feedback. 🔗 github.com/ankit02327/stock-price How It Started This project began from something I was personally learning: machine learning. While taking ML courses at university, I wanted to understand how the algorithms I was studying could be combined into a complete, practical application. That led me to build Stock Price Prediction around a real-world problem instead of keeping the work inside individual coursework exercises. The educational purpose has remained central. I want someone learning machine learning to be able to look at a real application, understand how different models are used, work with real financial data, experiment with the code, and eventually build projects of their own.
